Industry News: Can you be friends with your ex? What to consider first

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1438 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s your ex, sending a meme you would’ve laughed at together six months ago.
  • It has been revealed that moments like this are why staying friends with an ex can feel so confusing.
  • Whether you’re the one hoping to stay in touch or the one being asked to, here’s how to tell if staying friends would help you move on or make it harder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your phone buzzes. It’s your ex, sending a meme you would’ve laughed at together six months ago. You smile, then wonder why you smiled.

It has been revealed that moments like this are why staying friends with an ex can feel so confusing. For some people, staying connected feels natural because the habit, and maybe the care, is still there. For others, it makes healing feel harder. Every situation is different, and you’re allowed to take your time figuring out what works for you.

Whether you’re the one hoping to stay in touch or the one being asked to, here’s how to tell if staying friends would help you move on or make it harder.

Industry observers note that in some cases, you may be able to. Post-breakup friendships can be healthy and meaningful when the breakup was mutual, the relationship had little conflict, and both people have had time to grieve.

In a recent development, that said, every friendship between exes is different. Researchers who study friendships after breakups describe two kinds. In one, both people have moved on and value the connection. In the other, one or both people stay in touch because of lingering attraction or reluctance to end things. The first kind can be rewarding. The second can make it harder to get over the breakup.

In a recent development, the dynamic you had with your ex matters, too. A study found that relationships shaped by high conflict, emotional dependency, or attachment anxiety may be harder to turn into a friendship afterward.

In a recent development, before you decide anything, it may help to reflect on why you want to stay in touch. A few questions to sit with:.

What am I hoping this friendship gives me?

Am I trying to stay close to them or avoid the discomfort of letting go?

How would I feel if they started dating someone newly introduced?

If the last question stings, it may just mean that you need more time.

If you were the one who ended things, you might want friendship out of guilt or a wish to soften the loss. If you were the one who was left, you might view friendship as a potential path to getting back together.

Recent findings suggest that if the answers don’t come right away, try a mindfulness practice. A few minutes of reflection or a short breathing exercise can help you sort through what you’re thinking and feeling.

💙 Try the Pause to Check In meditation on the Calm app.

If you’ve thought it through and still want to stay in touch, a few signs suggest a friendship may work. People who are securely attached often find it easier to stay friends after a breakup, but the list below can apply to anyone:.

You both see the breakup as mutual, with no ongoing hurt, resentment, or blame.

You’ve both accepted that the romantic relationship is over, with no unresolved romantic feelings.

There’s a reason for the friendship beyond comfort or familiarity, such as shared values, kids together, or a work connection.

In certain cases, staying friends can make healing harder or keep you from pouring energy into newly introduced parts of your life:.

You’re still in love with your ex and hoping the friendship leads somewhere.

The relationship involved emotional manipulation, control, or abuse.

The friendship gets in the way of fresh relationships, like when a new partner feels uneasy about your connection.

You have different expectations for the friendship, which could leave one of you hurt.

💙 Discover the signs of having a toxic ex.

It can be, especially since staying in touch can make it harder to let go. One study found that regular contact with an ex may slow emotional recovery. When you’re still part of each other’s routines, it can be harder to mourn the end of the relationship.

By contrast, a low-contact friendship, where you talk occasionally and keep to limits you’ve agreed on, is less likely to hold either of you back.

How you feel after you talk is worth paying attention to. If you often feel sad, anxious, or unsettled, or you keep replaying the conversation, it may help to take some space.

💙 Read more on how to deal with a breakup when you’re hurting.

It may be appropriate to be friends with your ex, depending on your situation. It tends to work best when you’ve both moved on, the breakup didn’t involve harm, and the friendship fits both of your lives. If it also feels honest and comfortable to you, that’s a good sign.

Being friends with an ex isn’t automatically a red flag. If your partner is friends with an ex, how they handle it matters more than the friendship itself. A few questions to consider:.

Transparency: Do they talk about it openly, or does it feel secretive?

Priorities: Do they make time for you and the relationship?

Boundaries: Are there clear limits on the friendship, or does contact feel constant and undefined?

Responsiveness: When you raise a concern, does your partner listen or dismiss it?

If something doesn’t sit right, you could bring it up and see whether they listen, get defensive, or brush you off. If you’re the one staying friends with an ex, your fresh partner’s concerns are worth hearing out, even if nothing is wrong.

Recent findings suggest that you don’t have to keep in touch with your ex after a breakup. Taking space is often healthy and necessary, and you can change your mind later. You can choose a full break, a time-limited break (“let’s not talk for a few months”), or a low-contact friendship.

In a recent development, if you do stay in touch, some boundaries may protect your well-being. A few to consider:.

Set a pace. Daily texting can pull you back into old routines, so try starting with occasional check-ins instead.

Decide what’s off limits. That might mean dating lives, old conflicts, and late-night “remember when” talks.

Give yourself space online. Mute or unfollow for a while to adjust without ending the connection.

Recent findings suggest that strategy a review and a way out. After a few months, ask whether the friendship still feels good. If it doesn’t, have a line ready, like “I think I need to take a step back for now.”.

If you share children, a workplace, or a friend group, you may need to stay in touch. It’s often best to stick to logistics, like pickup times for the kids or project deadlines at work.

💙 Explore the Boundaries meditation on Calm.

There’s no set amount of time to wait before trying to be friends with an ex. Some people feel ready within months, while others take years. Some never feel ready or choose not to be friends, and that’s okay.

According to recent reports, A question to ask yourself is whether you can feel okay about the thought of your ex moving on. If that still hurts, you probably need more time.

Yes, being friends with an ex can sometimes turn into getting back together. Whether that’s a good thing depends on why your relationship ended and whether those reasons have changed.

In a recent development, problems tied to circumstances, like bad timing or distance, may be easier to work through than core differences, like values, long-term goals, or how you communicate. If you get back together and those core differences haven’t changed, the same patterns can resurface.

It’s painful when one of you wants to stay friends after a breakup and the other doesn’t, and what helps depends on which side you’re on.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re the one being asked, you’re allowed to say “not yet” or “no.” If you’re unsure, you don’t have to answer right away. You might say:.

“I care about you, and I need some time before I know what this looks like.”.

“Can we revisit this in a few months?”.

“I’m not able to be friends right now, and I hope you can respect that.”.

If you’re the one who wants friendship, the kindest move is to respect the space your ex has asked for. If you push for contact, it can get harder for you both to move on, even if giving them room hurts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two upcoming studies suggest autism and ADHD are becoming better recognized, not actually more prevalent, and that executive function and social challenges seen in both conditions actually stem from different underlying brain mechanisms.

ADHD and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) share overlapping symptoms, and prior studies suggest that nearly half of autistic children also have ADHD.1 Now, two latest studies on ADHD and ASD profiles suggest that rising diagnosis rates are a product of improved symptom recognition and diagnostic practices, and that executive function and social impairments seen in both ADHD and ASD may be traced to different cognitive pathways.

In a recent development, the first study, published in JAMA Psychiatry,2 evaluated the health records of 71,000 children and adolescents diagnosed with ADHD or ASD and 713,000 controls; it found that the annual number of individuals in the nationwide Danish health registry with newly diagnosed ADHD and/or ASD increased from 4,944 in 2012 to 9,179 in 2022. The proportion of girls diagnosed with ADHD or ASD and the median age at diagnosis also grew during the 10-year study period from 2012 to 2022.

However, traditional risk factors strongly linked to an ADHD or ASD diagnosis in 2012, such as low birth weight or lower household income, have become progressively less predictive with time. For example, children born with a low birth weight were 54% more likely to receive a subsequent diagnosis of ADHD or ASD in 2012; by 2022, that percentage dropped to 17%. Overall, the study found that children and adolescents diagnosed with ADHD or ASD today more closely resemble their neurotypical peers compared to those diagnosed 10 years ago.

These findings do not mean that ADHD or ASD has become less impairing; the spectrum of cases has shifted as clinicians get better at identifying less obvious cases. Greater awareness of ADHD and ASD, and broader access to diagnostic assessment tools, are also factors contributing to growing diagnoses among children.

In a recent development, “The study results do not show that these conditions are being overdiagnosed, or that they have become less severe,” states Oleguer Plana-Ripoll, Ph.D., a senior author of the study. “Rather, they indicate that the population receiving these diagnoses has changed over time, and this needs to be taken into account when interpreting current trends.”.

The second, smaller study, published in Frontiers in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry,3 found that executive functioning (EF) and social cognition (SC) impairments in children diagnosed with ADHD or ASD may look similar, but the impairments stem from different underlying mechanisms.

The cross-sectional, four-year study analyzed performance-based measures of 123 children, aged 6 to 11 years, across three matched groups: mild ASD, combined-type ADHD, and neurotypical peers.

Findings indicated that both ADHD and ASD groups performed worse than their neurotypical peers on measures of EF and SC. However, children with ADHD demonstrated weak social cognition due to difficulties with response inhibition and attention. Social cognition weaknesses in children with ASD, on the other hand, appeared to result from difficulties in understanding and interpreting social information.

More specifically, children in the ASD group performed significantly worse than children with ADHD on measures of:.

Children with ASD also displayed more difficulties than did children with ADHD on executive function tasks that measured the ability to shift between rules and adapt strategies.

Children in the ADHD group performed significantly worse than those in the ASD group on measures of:.

Sources indicate that how executive functions related to social cognition across disorders was the strongest indication of different cognitive processes between the two clinical groups. In the ADHD group, the theory-of-mind model explained 72% of the variance, compared to just 55% in the ASD group.

The researchers surmise that a person with ADHD relies heavily on executive functions, such as inhibition, auditory attention, and design fluency, for social cognition. In essence, their difficulties in social situations are not because they don’t understand social concepts but because distractions and impulsivity interfere.

In the ASD group, social difficulties were more likely to stem from affect recognition (understanding facial cues) and response set (cognitive flexibility, shifting perspectives), rather than from attention deficit or impulse control.

Sources indicate that “ADHD and autism are two separate and distinct conditions that happen to be found together much more frequently than would be expected by chance alone,” says ADHD expert William Dodson, M.D., LF-APA. “For people with co-existing ADHD and ASD, treating the ADHD is a means to an end. The world is a classroom for people with ASD, and they have to be ready to observe and practice what they’ve learned.”.

Results from the study suggest individuals would benefit more from targeted ADHD and ASD interventions matched to each disorder-specific profile rather than a single shared approach.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that world Children’s Day is a good moment for parents, caregivers, and teachers to ask kids how they’re feeling and listen without trying to fix anything.
  • Here’s a look at what the day is about, plus a few activities that can help kids feel understood, at home or in the classroom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA.

The backpack hits the floor, and "How was your day?" gets a one-word answer: "Fine." Kids don’t always say what’s on their mind, but a little time and attention may help them open up.

Recent findings suggest that world Children’s Day is a good moment for parents, caregivers, and teachers to ask kids how they’re feeling and listen without trying to fix anything. The day honors children’s rights, including the right to be heard.

Here’s a look at what the day is about, plus a few activities that can help kids feel understood, at home or in the classroom.

Sources indicate that world Children's Day is a global day of action for children, run by UNICEF. In 2026, it falls on Friday, November 20. This year’s theme is “My day. My rights. My future.” It invites children to tell world leaders what kind of future they want.

The day celebrates children and the rights they’re born with. In many places, children “take over” high-profile roles in media, sports, and government for the day. Landmarks light up blue to show support for children's rights.

November 20 marks two milestones for children’s rights. On this date in 1959, the UN General Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of the Child, a statement of shared ideals. Thirty years later to the day, it adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989, a treaty that nations can commit to follow.

The Convention sets out the rights every child has, including the right to be safe, to play, and to have their opinions taken seriously. Nearly every country has formally agreed to follow it, and it’s the most widely ratified human rights treaty in history.

Countries around the world mark World Children’s Day. Many also celebrate a separate Children’s Day, most notably June 1, International Children's Day.

Sources indicate that some countries do pick dates of their own. Turkey celebrates on April 23, and India on November 14. The dates differ, but the idea is the same: it’s a day dedicated to the youngest members of a community.

Industry observers note that you don’t need a substantial event to mark World Children’s Day. A meta-analysis on children and teens linked understanding emotions with better social skills and fewer behavior problems. Kids can build that understanding in everyday moments, like the ones below.

It has been revealed that kids may not know they have rights, but those who learn about them may feel more confident speaking up. UNICEF’s child-friendly version of the Convention explains the rights in plain language.

Try: Read one or two rights together, then ask which feels most important to them.

It has been revealed that not every child has the words for how they feel. Invite them to sketch their day from morning to night, then have them walk you through it.

Industry observers note that if they’re up for it, ask which part they loved most and which part felt hard. A drawing gives kids something concrete to point to as they talk, and that can feel easier than answering a broad question such as “How are you feeling?”.

Try: At home, pin the drawing to the fridge so your child can talk about it again if they’d like. In class, create an “Our Day” wall where kids can choose to share their drawings and spot the moments they had in common.

Sources indicate that when a child melts down, get curious about the feeling underneath. Help them put it into words: “It looks like you’re frustrated that it’s not your turn. Is that right?” Then listen carefully to their answer before you reassure them. “You’re fine” can sound dismissive, even when you mean well. When you talk about feelings this way, kids often learn to do it too.

Try: Post a chart of faces showing common feelings where kids can see it, and invite them to point to or say how they feel at the start of the day. Welcome any details they want to share.

💙 Once a major feeling has a name, here are coping skills for kids to try.

In a recent development, set aside a few minutes at dinner or morning circle time for everyone to share one high, one low, and one thing they’re thankful for. Take a turn yourself so kids feel more at ease sharing.

In a recent development, just listen as kids share, and try not to talk them out of a hard feeling. Kids tend to manage feelings better when you respond with warmth instead of brushing them off.

Try: Pass around a talking object, such as a small stuffed animal. Whoever holds it has the floor, grown-ups included.

💙 On Calm, listen to Feel Thankful With Thomas, a four-minute meditation for little ones, or the Gratitude session from the Classroom Mindfulness Tools series.

Recent findings suggest that A few minutes of meditation can be a soothing way for kids to slow down and settle. Sessions can focus on anything from breathing and body awareness to gratitude and kindness, so there’s room to follow your child’s interests or needs. Kids can sit, lie down, or stand, and they can stop whenever they’d like.

Try: Belly breathing is a gentle place to start. Have your child lie down with a stuffed animal on their belly and watch it rise and fall as they breathe slowly.

According to recent reports, 💙 Explore Calm’s Mindfulness for Kids sessions for ages 3–4, ages 5–6, ages 7–10, and ages 11–13. For little ones, try the Calm Your Worries With Percy meditation from the Thomas & Friends Learn to Meditate series.

Reading together gives you some time to connect, and stories can spark conversations about feelings. Kids may find it easier to talk about how a character feels than how they do.

Pick a book where a character is going through difficult feelings, then pause and ask, “What do you think she’s feeling?”.

Industry observers note that try: At home, make the story the last part of your child’s bedtime routine to help them wind down. In class, read a few pages at the end of the day.

World Children's Day is on Friday, November 20, 2026. It falls on the same date every year.

It has been revealed that the UNICEF theme for World Children’s Day 2026 is "My day. My rights. My future." It encourages children to share their hopes for the future with world leaders.

Recent findings suggest that the Convention on the Rights of the Child is the UN treaty behind the day. It names the rights every child has, including the right to be heard. For kids, it’s a written promise that their well-being and opinions count. Nearly every country has formally committed to it.

Recent findings suggest that no, World Children’s Day and International Children’s Day are two separate observances with similar goals. World Children's Day is UNICEF's celebration on November 20, while International Children's Day is the June 1 observance held in many countries. Both honor children and their rights, so you can mark either one or both.

The best World Children’s Day activities for kids are often simple ones, such as inviting them to draw their day, holding a family or classroom check-in, or reading a story together. You can do these activities wherever makes sense, and even a few minutes counts.

You can start with UNICEF’s child-friendly version of the Convention, and keep your explanation clear and specific. Try saying, “You have the right to feel safe, to play, and to say what you think.” Let them ask questions, and remind them that these rights belong to every child everywhere.

But the bechamel is great and it will get a bit thicker than just using cream. If you want that version, I’d just make the bechamel and add it at the end, using the same quantities as in this post: https://pinchofyum.com/crockpot-chicken-wild-rice-soup.

I prefer thighs because they stay a bit juicier, but chicken breasts can absolutely work. 🙂 I would pull them out of the sauce when they’re done and really kind of -chop them into shreddy chunks rather than straight shred them – maybe it’s just me, but I find that sometimes the shredding with chicken breasts can get a bit stringy.

Hi Lindsay, Thank you so much for all of your great recipes and ideas! I really appreciate all the hard work.

Lindsay – LOVE your recipes! Question about the freezer meals. There are a couple that you say you freeze the chicken separately but on the Chicken Wild Rice Soup it looks like you put the chicken in the same bag with everything. Can you please clarify for me? Thank you!!

Yes! 🙂 Short answer – you can put the chicken in the bag, or add it later. Either can work. 60 mindful Latest Year's resolution ideas to try in 2027

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5086 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we’ve all been there.
  • Then two weeks later, on a Wednesday, you have the most stressful day at your job and you find yourself pouring a huge glass of wine.
  • Resolutions don’t have to be this substantial set up for failure that feel impossible to keep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA.

Sources indicate that we’ve all been there. January 1st hits, and you decide this is the year you’re going to change your life and become the best version of yourself with some Upcoming Year’s resolutions. You might optimistically think, “You know what? I’m going to be healthier this year! I’m only going to drink on the weekends.”.

Then two weeks later, on a Wednesday, you have the most stressful day at your job and you find yourself pouring a huge glass of wine. You’re instantly filled with regret for breaking your resolution and vow to never do them again because they don’t work and are clearly designed to make you feel disappointed.

Take a deep breath. Resolutions don’t have to be this substantial set up for failure that feel impossible to keep. They can be as big or as small as you want them to be. We’ve put together a list of 60 mindful resolutions that are less about striving for perfection or making huge changes in your life, and more about slowly helping you to grow and build better habits in an achievable way. Sounds nice, right?

So let’s ditch our list of impossible goals and jump into 60 resolutions that could help you thrive in 2027.

At the end of the year, many of us step back and realize that we feel really disconnected from a lot of the people in our life. We get busy and stuck in our own little world. It’s too easy for connections with our family, friends, partners, or coworkers to dwindle from time to time.

If this sounds familiar, here are 15 resolutions that can help you build more fulfilling relationships so that your support networks are there for you when you need it. (And you’re there for them when they need it too.).

In a recent development, pro tip: you don’t need to do all of 15. Just try choosing a few that feel good to you and then take some small steps towards adding them into your routine.

Sources indicate that make a habit of giving your full attention to the people who matter most to you. Try planning regular (or semi-regular) family dinners, date nights, or hangs with friends. If you like phone calls, those work great too. (Just make sure you’re fully present!).

When someone’s talking to you, focus fully on what they’re saying instead of thinking about your reply or what you’re going to eat for your next meal (we’ve all been there). Active listening shows respect to your loved one and can help deepen your bond. If you want to get better at active listening, here are eight techniques to help.

According to recent reports, too often, we take those around us for granted, so let the people in your life know you appreciate them. Saying something as easy as, “thank you” or writing a cute little note can let your loved one know how much they mean to you and make them feel good. Who doesn’t want to make their loved one feel good?

According to recent reports, if you love them, say it. Life’s too short! Telling someone you love them is powerful and can help you grow a stronger bond. If you have people in your life like a macho uncle or disengaged cousin who have a hard time saying I love you, be the first to jump in and show them that it’s okay to express your affection for one another.

It has been revealed that if you notice someone struggling in your life, step in and help. It doesn't need to be revolutionary. It could be helping with laundry or simply being there to listen. Just letting them know that you see their efforts and want to help can make a huge difference.

Industry observers note that relationships are work. And in order for them to work, you need to put time into them. So set a reminder to check in with your loved ones, especially the ones you don’t see often. A quick text or call can do the trick and help you stay connected with your favorite people. And if you have folks in your life who are struggling, or who experience loneliness, make an extra effort to reach out and show you care.

Recent findings suggest that don’t let misunderstandings grow. When you’re upset with someone, bring it up to them calmly and kindly, and with the goal of finding a solution. It can help to lead with “I feel” statements. And if your feelings are hurt over an innocent misunderstanding, start with, “I know you didn’t mean to hurt my feelings but,” so the other person knows they’re not in trouble and you want to come to a place of understanding.

Sources indicate that this might sound obvious, but if your loved one has good news, show genuine excitement for the good things that are happening for them. We all feel good when others celebrate with us. So send those flowers — almost no one’s going to get mad at you for sending flowers. Sometimes celebrating success for others feels hard if you feel stuck in your life, but by genuinely finding happiness for others, you may feel the glow of that happiness yourself.

In a recent development, use conversions with others as a time to genuinely disconnect from technology and focus on being together. When you’re spending time with someone, keep your phone in your pocket, in your purse, or somewhere that’s not in your hand. Give your loved one your full attention. This will make them feel seen and it helps you to stay more in the moment and form deeper connections.

Industry observers note that everyone loves to feel seen and valued. Sometimes just surprising someone you love with a small gesture can make their day. It doesn’t have to be major, it could just be showing up to a hang with your loved one’s favorite snack, their preferred coffee drink, or even a small bouquet of flowers. Trying to be better about budgeting? Handwritten cards, or homemade crafts also make lovely surprises.

Industry observers note that when someone you care about is struggling, before reacting, take a moment to put yourself in their shoes and understand what they might be going through. This can be a lot easier noted than done, but try to treat them the way you would want to be treated —  with kindness instead of judgment.

💙 If Empathy doesn’t come easy for you, check out this meditation from Tamara Levitt’s Relationships with Others series.

We all have preferences for how we like to give and receive love and it’s so special when the people in our lives make an effort to communicate affection in the ways we most appreciate. So take some time to understand a partner, family member, or friends love languages (here’s an overview of all five and how to identify yours). Showing love in the ways they like can make you closer. (And probably earn you brownie points!).

Recent findings suggest that say yes to an invite or an activity you wouldn’t normally do. Stepping out of your comfort zone can help you feel energized and open you up to new experiences and learnings about yourself. The one time when it’s okay not to say yes is if you’re establishing boundaries with your emotional energy or time. It’s all about balance!

According to recent reports, while saying yes is great (see above), saying no is also key. Make an effort to have healthy relationships with solid boundaries. Tell people what you need, like alone time or limits on work talk. And respect their boundaries too. If all of that sounds tough, check out these six tips to setting healthy boundaries in your relationships.

In a recent development, humans make mistakes and the best thing you can do is to acknowledge them, learn and grow. So try to take responsibility if you make a mistake. You’ll feel free of guilt and you won’t have to double down on something you probably didn’t mean to do in the first place (like a bad joke that hurt someone’s feelings, or a meeting you were super late for.) A heartfelt apology can mend any damage and show your maturity (these seven tips will help you do it).

Doesn’t it feel like we’re always trying to find a better work-life balance, get promoted, improve our work ethic, and feel more fulfilled with the work we’re doing? That constant desire for some sort of growth or change can be overwhelming and leave you not knowing where to start.

So we’ve put together 15 work resolutions that might be more sustainable and rewarding for you — and will hopefully make the whole process feel less overwhelming.

Recent findings suggest that protecting your personal time is so important for avoiding burnout, so decide on clear work hours and stick to them. Try setting a goal for logging off by 6pm or not looking at emails in your off time. If your job doesn’t at the moment give you the freedom to set these boundaries, chat with your superiors and express your goals where work-life balance is concerned.

Organize your workspace to reduce clutter. A working area that you like (or at least doesn’t cause more stress) can really improve your mood and your focus. Once you reduce the clutter and get rid of any items that aren’t sparking joy, you could mindfully add things that feel good like a plant, photo, or a comfy chair.

Large projects can be overwhelming. Try breaking them down into smaller, more manageable steps to make them less daunting and help you stay on track. You can also practice time-boxing to keep your focus — here’s how to do it .

Go for a five-minute walk, enjoy a cup or tea, or do a quick stretch. It doesn’t really matter what you do on a break, just that you do something to rest your mind and give your body a little love. Set reminders if it’ll help you remember. (Here are 20 ways to take a mindful break.).

Sources indicate that start each day by identifying your top three priorities. If you focus on the most important tasks first, this will help you make progress where it matters most. Got a few things on your to-do list that aren’t time sensitive? Resist the temptation to try to get them done when you’re exhausted and bump them to tomorrow when you can focus.

Just like you want to celebrate the achievements of the people in your life, it’s equally crucial to celebrate yourself! Take note of all of your accomplishments. This can help boost your confidence, help you stay motivated, and even make you smile.

In a recent development, making fresh friends isn’t just for your school years. Make an effort to connect with coworkers or other people in your field. Getting coffee with colleagues can help you build relationships and even help with career growth. You might find that your career is more fulfilling when you have solid relationships with colleagues and coworkers.

Work on being clear and concise in emails, meetings, and in conversations. Practicing good communication not only improves your productivity but also helps avoid misunderstandings (these 13 tips can help).

According to recent reports, if you’re overwhelmed and juggling too much, look for tasks that can be given to others to make your life easier. This doesn’t mean you’re not good at your job. It just means you're making sure your energy is spent where it’s needed most.

Struggling to focus? Single-tasting is where it’s at. Take on one task at a time and not five at once. This will improve the quality of your work and help you feel less like you want to scream.

Recent findings suggest that even if it’s scary, seek out feedback from your boss, coworkers, or clients. Constructive input can help you get better and show that you want to improve. Just make sure you’re also receiving feedback for things you’re doing well, not just areas where you could do better.

Recent findings suggest that find a method that helps you stay on top of deadlines. A to-do list app, a daily planner, or a bullet journal could help keep track of all your tasks. Explore some different ideas to find what works best for you.

Recent findings suggest that don’t hesitate to ask for what you need. If anything, this can help you get taken more seriously and help with career growth. Ask for that raise, request that more flexible schedule, tell your boss you need additional resources to complete that project.

💙 Learn how to practice Speaking Up at work with this session from the Mindful Leadership Wisdom Series.

Sources indicate that set goals that align with your long-term dreams and values, not just what you hope to achieve. These could be around building confidence, becoming a more mindful leader, or exploring a newly introduced field you’ve always been interested in.

Sources indicate that when you don’t feel mentally like you’re firing on all cylinders, it can be tough to even think of what to focus on to help your mental health. We get it — you’re probably already stressed, so making a decision on a resolution to be less stressed might be the last thing you want to (or can) do.

To help you out, we put together a list of 15 small and intentional resolutions that will help nurture your mind and create space for calm and joy in 2027.

Industry observers note that (Psst: You don’t have to do all of them. Start with one or two that’ll help you feel more balanced, calm, and connected, and then go from there.).

Sources indicate that write down and reflect on your thoughts, feelings, and experiences each day. This can help you process your emotions and recognize some patterns you have. Journaling is also a great way to practice gratitude.

It has been revealed that each day, take a moment to think of three things you’re grateful for. This can rewire your brain to look for the positives in your life. It doesn’t have to be getting a promotion or finding your perfect partner, it can be as small as not burning your bagel today. If you want to find more ways to incorporate gratitude into your days, here are eight ideas to get you started.

Spend a few minutes a day practicing mindfulness. And while this could be a five minute meditation, it could also be a bit of deep breathing on a work break, or just noticing the sights and sounds on your morning walk. Any moment where you become fully present counts!

Industry observers note that go to bed and wake up at the same time every day to help you get better quality sleep (here are six more tips to help you get those Zzzzs). The more rested you are, the more you’ll be able to handle the stress that comes up throughout the day.

Sources indicate that nature has a way of calming us down and recharging us, so if it’s possible, try to get outside everyday. It doesn't have to be a big hike, it can be as simple as walking around your block or even just going into your yard.

This is a major one! Try to gradually reduce the time you spend on your phone, computer, or watching TV, especially before bed. You could read that novel that’s been on your bedside table for ever or catch up with a loved one instead. But take it slow, we know it’s not easy.

Give yourself permission to say no to things that overwhelm or overcommit you. It’s more key to protect your energy than to burn yourself out trying to please other people. If saying no is hard for you, here’s 30 ways to do it nicely.

Recent findings suggest that get in the habit of reaching out to a loved one or a therapist when you’re feeling stressed or overwhelmed. Talking about our feelings can help us feel lighter and even give us a fresh perspective.

A clean environment isn’t just for your desk. Having a clean home can calm you too. So take some small steps to organize your home. You might try doing just one room at a time, it doesn’t need to be all at once.

Schedule regular breaks so you don’t have a meltdown. These pauses can really help you reduce your stress and keep you focused. Grabbing a glass of water, breathing deeply, or gently stretching can all help reset you and give your mind a moment to rest.

In a recent development, treat yourself the way you would your closest friend. Avoid going in on yourself with harsh, critical thoughts and instead say some sweet nothings to yourself. We know this isn’t always easy, so here are eight tips to help you quiet that inner critic.

Start a hobby that lets you express yourself. This can be therapeutic and put you in a better mood. Ever been curious about painting or playing music? Maybe now’s your chance to explore that curiosity.

Exercising relieves a lot of stress. But you don’t need to spend hours at the gym or set some big weight loss goal. Instead, try out a newly introduced yoga class, have a dance party in your living room, or find other ways to move your body that feel nourishing to you.

Recent findings suggest that go easy on yourself, you don’t need to be perfect (newsflash: there’s no such thing). It can help to focus on all the small ways you're growing each day, not on the destination. Sometimes it’s better to think about growth-setting instead of goal setting.

Don’t regularly spend your time on something that drains your energy. Seek out places that bring you positivity instead. If certain people you hang around with make you feel bad, limit your exposure to them. This might look like setting boundaries with family about how many events you attend each year, or with friends by limiting how much you talk or get together.

💙 If you’re looking for more positivity in your life, learn how to Process and Move Past Negativity during the Overcome Stress and Anxiety series with Dr. Julie Smith.

Industry observers note that okay, let’s face it. Most of us want to look and feel our best — and there’s nothing wrong with that. But better physical health is also about feeling energized, staying strong, and giving our body the help it needs to thrive.

In a recent development, we don’t need to tell you that working out consistently is a lot easier mentioned than done. Sure, in a perfect world, we always have the time and energy to get to the gym. But we don’t live in that world. We have endless responsibilities and working out might be the first thing to go when we’re busy.

So explore these 15 manageable resolutions that can help you feel strong and energized going into 2027. And remember, you don’t need to force yourself to go all-in on physical wellness to feel better. Just start with one or two that feel like they’d be easier to make a consistent habit and go from there.

Recent findings suggest that aim for some form of movement every day –– it doesn’t have to be intense. Try a 10–minute stretch or a brisk walk through your favorite part of your neighborhood. Focus on what makes you feel good in your body, which may change day to day.

Industry observers note that hydration makes you feel good and stay alert, so try to aim for 8–10 glasses of water a day. Carry a reusable water bottle with you to make it easier to hit your goal and remind you to drink. If regular water feels boring try adding slices of your favorite citrus or fresh mint to your water.

Add a rainbow of foods to your plate! Focus on eating a mix of fruits, veggies, lean proteins, and whole grains. Try meal prepping ahead of time to make it easier for you to choose healthy options. Bonus points if you try to stay mindful while you cook and while you eat — here’s how.

Industry observers note that swap out processed snacks for healthier options like fruit, nuts, seeds, or yogurt. Try keeping nutritious snacks nearby to make it easier to avoid reaching your favorite sweets. With that in mind, don’t forget that dark chocolate has some antioxidants so adding a few dark chocolate chips to your trail mix is a-okay with us!

When you sleep better, you feel better. End of story. Aim for around eight hours of quality sleep each night. It can help to have a wind down routine at the end of your day to help your body know that it’s time for rest. These nine steps can help you create a calming bedtime routine.

If you are able to take stairs instead of elevators or escalators, go for it! Making small, active choices throughout your day to help you get a little more movement. You could also try parking farther away to get in a few extra steps.

Add some stretching into your daily routine to improve your flexibility, reduce your tension, and prevent injuring yourself. Try stretching for a few minutes as soon as you get out of bed or right before you get into bed — here are seven we like.

We know it can be frustrating or scary to go see a doctor, but don’t wait to see one until you feel sick. Set up your physicals and dental cleanings so that you can breathe easy and not worry about your health. You’ll be proud of yourself when you leave that doctor’s office!

Recent findings suggest that generally, it’s recommended to cut back on foods high in sugar. You may be surprised how much sugar some of your daily go-tos have, so stay mindful of what you’re consuming (you could check the labels for sugar content if that works for you).. It’s not about never having a treat, but bringing more awareness to what you’re eating and how it’s making you feel. It’s all about balance.

Industry observers note that working out can really feel like work a lot of the time. So shake up your routine to help keep you excited to exercise. Ever tried kickboxing or swimming? Maybe 2027 is the year you hop in the boxing ring or jump in the pool.

According to recent reports, if you have a desk job, try to stand up and move every hour. Consider switching to a standing desk if that’s an option. If you work from home and have space for a walking pad in front of a standing desk you can also get your steps in while you work.

We know that the newly introduced year isn’t always the time you want to get outside for a walk, but sunshine and time in nature can boost your mood. If you live in the northern hemisphere, bundle up and try going for a walk, run, or bike ride outside whenever the weather allows it.

Industry observers note that if you drink alcohol, consider cutting back by a few drinks or setting limits. It can help to have fun or festive swap, so try sipping on flavored sparkling water or a mocktail at a social event or as a treat at the end of a long week. Sometimes creating a special drink that’s free of booze creates the same excitement as making a special cocktail. And you might love the way you feel the next morning when you’re hydrating your body with your evening beverage instead of dehydrating it.

Good posture helps prevent back and neck pain so pay attention to how you sit and stand. And add exercises that focus on strengthening your core into your workout. This will help support better alignment. Sitting at a desk for work? Set alarms every so often to remind you to stand up and stretch.

Industry observers note that celebrating your progress helps you to keep going — we all need a good pat on the back. If you drink an extra glass of water or walk an extra mile, take note of it. Maybe even do a little happy dance. If you go for a walk four days in a row, make a note in your journal or notebook. The more you celebrate your progress the prouder of yourself you’ll be (and the easier it is to keep it up).

💙 Learn how to celebrate the Small Wins on the path to achieving your larger goals with help from Jay Shetty.

According to recent reports, new Year’s resolutions are personal goals or promises you make to yourself at the start of a new year. They can be about anything and it’s entirely up to you. They can be big like training for a marathon or small like drinking more water.

Sources indicate that usually people use it as a chance to reflect, change up some patterns in their life, and start fresh. If you’re looking to set a resolution but don’t know where to start, here are five areas people tend to focus on:.

You don’t have to make resolutions to have a wonderful upcoming year. But if you want to try, keep in mind that resolutions work best when you make them work for you. So yes — resolutions matter if you use them as a tool to help you live with more purpose and joy, then you’ll set yourself up for more success.

When you’re setting your resolutions, focus on what would make you feel happier, healthier and more fulfilled and go from there. And approach resolutions with kindness and flexibility, especially if you don’t end up following through on one.

Industry observers note that if the idea of resolutions feels overwhelming — we get it. Here’s three ways that could make it easier for you:.

Focus on one word or theme for the year that feels right to you, like “balance” or “growth.”.

Set a small monthly intention instead of a year-long commitment.

Celebrate progress instead of perfection by noticing little wins along the way.

Recent findings suggest that we wish there were five magical resolutions that could solve all of our problems at once. But unfortunately there’s no such thing. What we can tell you is the most successful resolutions tend to be the ones that feel right to you.

According to recent reports, it’s key to focus on the right area when setting your resolution, so you’ll be more likely to stick with them. Here are five areas to focus on when setting your resolution:.

Resolutions that focus on building stronger relationships — Pick ones that’ll fill you up and add more joy to your life.

Resolutions that focus on taking care of your physical health — Pick ones that focus on regular exercise, better nutrition, or improved sleep.

Resolutions that focus on your mental health — Pick ones that practice gratitude or mindfulness, so that they can help you feel calmer and more balanced.

Resolutions that focus on your career –– Pick ones that focus on learning a upcoming skill or creating a better work-life balance so that your professional life can become more rewarding.

Resolutions that focus on personal growth –– Pick ones that focus on starting fresh hobbies or giving back to your community.

All of us at one point or another have probably failed at a resolution we’ve set for ourselves. And when that happens, it can feel pretty disappointing. But resolutions can work — if you set them in the right way.

Resolutions that are vague or overly ambitious tend to be a recipe for failure. But if you set ones that are realistic and meaningful to you, it’ll be a lot easier to keep your resolution and see the change you want. But remember to be flexible and kind to yourself. We’re all not perfect and mistakes happen. So try not to beat yourself up if you don’t stick to your goals perfectly. Focus on progress, not perfection.

If you find it easier to set monthly intentions as opposed to setting one year-long resolution, go for that. Tailor the resolutions so they work best for you.

In a recent development, sometimes the minute we think of resolutions, we can get sad or overwhelmed at the baggage of our past failed resolutions. If this is you — we understand. Resolutions aren’t for everyone. But if you’re interested, there are other ways you can focus on self-improvement and growth.

In a recent development, if a long list of goals is too daunting for you, try picking a single word to guide your year. You could use words like “balance,” or “connection,” to remind yourself to make choices that match with your values.

If setting smaller, short-term goals might help you to stay motivated, you could try focusing on building better sleep habits in January, and then shifting to something like improving your diet in February.

Industry observers note that if tracking your progress will make it more fun for you and help you to invest more, try using a habit tracker app, or even just a calendar. This way it’ll be easier to celebrate your little wins along the way.

Resolutions that focus on relationships can bring more connection, understanding, and happiness into your life. And a good way to show the people you love the most how much they mean to you is to set a resolution to spend more quality time with them.

According to recent reports, acts of kindness also go a long way to strengthen your relationships. So if this is key to you, try setting an intention to express gratitude more often, like thanking your partner for their support.

It has been revealed that you could also set a resolution to unplug more often. This can help free up your time and create more meaningful, distraction-free moments with the people you care about the most.

Mental health is hard. Getting support doesn't have to be. The Calm app puts the tools to feel better in your back pocket, with personalized content to manage stress and anxiety, get better sleep, and feel more present in your life.

When Your Body’s Operating System Glitches

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (422 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Additudemag

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The autonomic nervous system regulates everything from heart rate to digestion.
  • You probably don’t give much thought to how your heart speeds up during exercise or how blood continues flowing to your brain when you stand up.
  • The autonomic nervous system controls heart rate, blood pressure, the digestive process, body temperature, and continuous blood circulation in the presence of gravity — squeezing blood out of the legs and torso and redistributing it to the head and heart when you move from lying down or sitting to standing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The autonomic nervous system regulates everything from heart rate to digestion. Abnormalities may contribute to ADHD and POTS symptoms.

You probably don’t give much thought to how your heart speeds up during exercise or how blood continues flowing to your brain when you stand up. These essential functions are managed by the autonomic nervous system, the body’s complex operating system, which runs quietly in the background.

The autonomic nervous system controls heart rate, blood pressure, the digestive process, body temperature, and continuous blood circulation in the presence of gravity — squeezing blood out of the legs and torso and redistributing it to the head and heart when you move from lying down or sitting to standing.

According to recent reports, some studies suggest that autonomic nervous system abnormalities may contribute to ADHD symptoms like inattention and impulsiveness. Clinicians may notice and use these symptoms to diagnose ADHD, but the underlying cause might reflect atypical autonomic nervous system activity.

Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS) is an atypical or malfunctioning state of the autonomic nervous system. People with ADHD and/or hypermobility appear to have a higher prevalence of POTS than do members of the general population. Symptoms include dizziness or fainting when standing up from a sitting or lying position due to sudden changes in blood pressure and heart rate.

[Read: ADHD’s Curious Connections to Chronic Inflammation and Dysautonomia].

In individuals with hypermobility, autonomic dysregulation may be caused by irritation of the nerves that are intermittently stretched due to lax ligaments at the craniocervical junction, where the brain and upper spine meet.

A tilt table test, which measures your heart rate and blood pressure as you change position, is the main way POTS is diagnosed. Other assessments include blood and urine tests and a measure of the autonomic nerves that control sweating.

[Read: Exploring the ADHD-Inflammation Link].

A living trust is a legal arrangement where you (the grantor) transfer ownership of your assets to a trust entity that you also control (as trustee). It sounds circular, and in practice, during your lifetime, nothing changes about how you use your money and property. The magic happens when you die or become incapacitated.

The three key roles in a living trust:.

During your lifetime: You are both the grantor and the trustee. You control everything. You can add or remove assets, change beneficiaries, modify terms, or dissolve the trust entirely. Your Social Security number is the trust's tax ID — there is no separate tax return. For practical purposes, nothing changes about your daily financial life.

In a recent development, if you become incapacitated: Your successor trustee immediately takes over management of trust assets. No court petition needed. No guardianship proceeding. No delay. This is a major advantage over a will, which provides zero protection during incapacity.

When you die: Your successor trustee distributes assets according to your trust document. No probate court. No public record. No waiting 6-18 months. Beneficiaries can typically receive assets within days or weeks.

A living trust essentially creates a private, self-executing transfer system that operates outside the court system entirely. For FI families who have spent years building wealth, this means your heirs receive the full value of your estate without probate eating into it.

According to recent reports, the terms "revocable" and "irrevocable" describe whether you can change or dissolve the trust after creating it. This distinction has major implications for control, taxes, and asset protection.

Revocable living trust — the standard choice for most families:.

Recent findings suggest that you retain full control. You can amend the trust, add or remove assets, change beneficiaries, or dissolve it completely at any time. Because you maintain control, the IRS treats trust assets as yours — they are included in your taxable estate, and creditors can reach them. The primary benefit is probate avoidance and incapacity protection, not asset protection or tax reduction.

Irrevocable trust — the advanced tool for specific situations:.

Once created, you generally cannot change or revoke it. You give up control of the assets placed inside. In exchange, you get benefits that a revocable trust cannot provide.

When an irrevocable trust makes sense:.

Industry observers note that for most FI families: A revocable living trust is the right starting point. It provides the two biggest benefits — probate avoidance and incapacity protection — while letting you maintain complete control.

The re-titling process for real estate: This is the most critical step and requires recording a new deed. You transfer ownership from "John Smith" to "John Smith, Trustee of the John Smith Revocable Living Trust dated January 15, 2024." Contact your county recorder's office or have your attorney prepare the deed. Most counties charge $15-$75 for recording. Notify your mortgage firm (they cannot call the loan due under the Garn-St. Germain Act for transfers to a revocable trust) and your homeowners insurance carrier.

Ongoing funding discipline: Every time you open a new bank account, buy property, or acquire significant assets, ask: "Should this be titled in my trust?" Create a simple checklist and review it annually. The most common estate planning failure is a perfectly drafted trust with assets still titled in the grantor's personal name.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

It has been revealed that A common concern is whether transferring your home into a trust triggers a due-on-sale clause in your mortgage. Under the federal Garn-St. Germain Depository Institutions Act of 1982, lenders cannot accelerate a mortgage when property is transferred to a revocable trust where the borrower remains a beneficiary and occupant. This protection applies to residential properties with fewer than five units. Your lender may ask for a copy of the trust document, but they cannot call the loan. Always notify your homeowners insurance manufacturer of the title change to ensure coverage remains valid.

A living trust is most valuable if your net worth exceeds $500K, you own property in multiple states, you want to avoid probate, or you want incapacity protection. If your estate is simple and under $500K, a will may be sufficient.

Online services (Trust & Will $399-$599, LegalZoom $399-$599) work for simple trusts. For complex situations or estates over $1M, an estate planning attorney ($1,500-$5,000) ensures proper drafting and funding.

Sources indicate that your trust document should name your trustee (you), successor trustee, beneficiaries, and detailed distribution instructions. Include provisions for incapacity and specific instructions for each major asset category.

According to recent reports, transfer real estate by recording newly introduced deeds. Retitle bank and brokerage accounts into the trust name. Complete the assignment of personal property document. This is the most critical step — an unfunded trust is useless.

It has been revealed that draft a pour-over will that directs any assets not in the trust to pour into it upon your death. This will also names guardians for minor children. Review and patch both documents every 3-5 years.

It has been revealed that A living trust is a legal entity you create during your lifetime that holds your assets. You serve as trustee and maintain full control. When you die or become incapacitated, a successor trustee you named manages and distributes assets to your beneficiaries — without probate or court involvement.

A revocable living trust costs $1,500-$3,000 through an estate planning attorney, or $399-$599 through online services like Trust & Will or LegalZoom. Irrevocable trusts cost $3,000-$10,000+ due to their complexity. Additional costs include deed preparation ($200-$500) for transferring real estate.

Industry observers note that A revocable living trust does NOT reduce estate taxes — assets are still part of your taxable estate because you maintain control. Only irrevocable trusts remove assets from your taxable estate. However, with the federal estate tax exemption at $13.61 million per individual (2024), estate taxes only affect very large estates.

Yes, and you should be. With a revocable living trust, you serve as your own trustee during your lifetime. You maintain complete control over all trust assets — buying, selling, spending, and investing exactly as you did before. Your successor trustee only takes over upon your death or incapacity.

A will goes through probate court (public, 6-18 months, costs 3-7% of estate). A living trust avoids probate entirely (private, days to weeks, minimal cost). A trust also provides incapacity protection, which a will does not. However, a will can name guardians for minor children, which a trust cannot.

Sources indicate that yes. You need a pour-over will to catch any assets not titled in the trust and to name guardians for minor children. The trust handles your major assets and avoids probate. The will serves as a safety net for everything else.

It has been revealed that A living trust is one of the most effective tools for protecting the wealth you have built on the path to financial independence. It avoids probate, provides incapacity protection, maintains complete privacy, and ensures your heirs receive assets promptly and efficiently. The key is actually funding the trust — transferring asset titles into it. For FI families with a net worth above $500K, the $1,500-$5,000 setup cost pays for itself many times over in avoided probate fees and time savings for your heirs.

#103858. How to love yourself: 7 steps to learn self-love

How to love yourself: 7 steps to learn self-love

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3379 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Learning how to love yourself can feel unfamiliar—especially if your inner voice leans more critical than kind.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you’ve ever asked yourself, “How do I love myself?” or wondered what the actual meaning of self-love is, you’re not alone.
  • Developing self-love doesn’t mean you’re selfish or self-centered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, CDCES, MBA.

Learning how to love yourself can feel unfamiliar—especially if your inner voice leans more critical than kind. But here’s the truth: self-love isn’t something you’re born knowing how to do. It’s something you learn. And like any meaningful practice, it takes time, intention, and a lot of patience.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve ever asked yourself, “How do I love myself?” or wondered what the actual meaning of self-love is, you’re not alone. Many of us were never taught how to speak to ourselves with compassion, how to set boundaries that honor our needs, or how to practice everyday self-respect. That’s where this guide comes in—because it’s never too late to build a more loving relationship with yourself.

Developing self-love doesn’t mean you’re selfish or self-centered. It means learning to treat yourself the way you’d treat someone you care deeply about—with gentleness, understanding, and care. Whether you’re struggling with self-worth, navigating difficult emotions, or simply trying to reconnect with the real you, these seven steps offer a foundation for how to practice self-love in real, actionable ways.

Recent findings suggest that from building self-awareness and setting healthy boundaries to practicing forgiveness and celebrating your wins, this guide is here to support your growth. Start small, stay consistent, and trust that loving yourself is not only possible—it’s one of the most empowering things you’ll ever do.

Self-love is exactly how it sounds—it’s a love for yourself and having an interest in your own well-being and happiness. Loving yourself doesn’t mean being self-centered or selfish. It’s about forming a caring relationship with yourself, like getting to know a good friend.

The idea of loving yourself isn’t just a ‘feel-good’ concept—it’s essential for mental health. Research indicates that self-compassion is linked to lower stress, reduced anxiety, and even improved physical health. People who actively practice self-love tend to set better boundaries, build stronger relationships, and experience less burnout.

According to recent reports, self-love is vital because the relationship you have with yourself sets the tone for how you deal with every aspect of life: your bonds with others, the way you handle challenges, and how you celebrate joys. When you’re kind and understanding toward yourself, you’re better equipped to navigate life’s ups and downs.

It has been revealed that but how do you start loving yourself? Where do you even begin? Self-love starts with understanding where you stand right now. Take a look at your current feelings toward your mental health, motivation, and overall well-being. Are you harsh with yourself when things don’t go as planned? Do you forget to celebrate your wins, especially the small ones? These little check-ins can pave the path to walking toward self-love.

Loving yourself isn’t a switch you turn on or off. It’s a practice that takes time, commitment, and, well, practice, to cultivate. For many of us, the idea of loving ourselves feels out of reach. That’s why it’s often helpful to break the concept of self-love down into its distinctive elements — including self-trust, self-compassion, and self-awareness.

This can make it easier to start developing a self-love practice that feels achievable and manageable. So instead of viewing self-love as something you have to win at, try practicing these seven steps.

Self-awareness: Understand your feelings, thoughts, and behaviors.

Self-expression: Be true to who you are in all areas of life.

Self-care: Take care of your body and mind.

Self-trust: Believe in your ability to handle life’s ups and downs.

Self-compassion: Be kind to yourself, especially when times are tough.

Self-respect: Honor your worth by setting healthy boundaries.

Self-acceptance: Embrace who you are, including the parts you don’t find perfect. Remember what we said about perfection?

Sources indicate that sometimes practicing self-love means taking action or establishing boundaries to protect your mental health. Here are a few IRL examples of how you can practice self-love today.

Industry observers note that prioritize rest to recharge: Imagine you’ve had a long week, and instead of squeezing in one more task, you decide to turn off your devices and enjoy a full night’s sleep. Studies have shown that adequate rest improves mood, cognitive function, and emotional resilience​. By honoring your body’s need for recovery, you demonstrate that you value your well-being above productivity.

Say no to unhealthy relationships: Picture being invited to a gathering where you know that certain individuals drain your energy. Choosing to decline isn't selfish; it’s self-preservation. Healthy boundaries are key to having self-respect and healthy relationships. Saying no clears space for connections that truly nourish you​.

In a recent development, practice forgiveness for yourself: Maybe you’ve made a mistake at work and feel embarrassed. Instead of spiraling into self-criticism, try acknowledging the error, learning from it, and moving on. Self-compassion may help reduce anxiety and create more resilience, helping you recover more effectively from setbacks​. Mistakes are normal, and it’s all about “failing up”.

It has been revealed that create moments of mindfulness amid the chaos: Let’s say your day is hectic, and stress feels overwhelming. This is the moment to pause for a brief grounding exercise (here’s one of our favorites). Maybe you focus on your breath or tune into your surroundings. These types of practice not only calm your nervous system but also remind you of your ability to care for yourself even in small, meaningful ways​.

Treat yourself with the same kindness you show others: When you reflect on a recent accomplishment—major or small—you choose to celebrate it instead of brushing it off. There are huge benefits to recognizing your personal achievements. Giving yourself a pat on the back may help boost self-esteem and even long-term happiness​.

Self-love can feel unfamiliar and challenging to some of us, particularly if we’ve got into a habit of being hard on ourselves. The steps above can help break down the idea of self-love into more manageable elements.

But what practical things can we do to cultivate practices like self-awareness and self-trust? We got you. For each of the self-love steps, we’re sharing tools, techniques and exercises you can use to help get you closer to loving yourself.

Building self-awareness helps cultivate self-love by giving you further insight into what makes you who you are on an emotional level. Begin by tuning into your thoughts and feelings.

It has been revealed that what makes you feel happy, sad, or excited? Then, take it a step further. What makes you feel overwhelmed, overjoyed, or anxious? Knowing yourself is the first step to loving yourself.

Practice mindfulness: Try mindfulness practices to stay present and understand your thoughts and feelings better.

Educate yourself: Empower yourself through education by reading books, attending workshops, or engaging in discussions that promote self-awareness, self-compassion, and self-love.

Recent findings suggest that schedule regular self-check-ins: Reflect on your feelings, goals, and progress. Write them down, and revisit them often.

Tune into yourself through meditation: Spend some quiet time meditating to help declutter your mind and tap into your desires.

Let go of what no longer serves you: Let go of old habits or relationships that no longer contribute to your growth or happiness. We know this practice can be difficult, but removing what no longer brings you joy makes space for the good to come in.

💙 If you want to learn to relate to your thoughts in a healthier way, press play on Shift Your Perspective with Jay Shetty.

Loving yourself also means giving yourself permission to express your thoughts and feelings both inwardly and outwardly. Express yourself honestly in your day-to-day life. Be true to who you are, whether you’re simply chatting with friends or making big decisions at work.

Engage in creative expression: Whether it's drawing, writing, or any other form of creative expression, allowing your creativity to flow freely can become an act of self-love.

Recent findings suggest that discover newly introduced hobbies: Explore new activities that bring you joy and allow you to express yourself. Have you always wanted to try your hand at a group sport or acting? Now’s the time to try.

Journaling: Write down your thoughts, feelings, and experiences daily, and don’t hold back. Expressing yourself through writing can be cathartic and a helpful step in falling back in love with who you are.

Spend quality time with yourself: Enjoy your own manufacturer by doing things that make you happy. There’s a difference between doing something alone and feeling lonely. Embracing solo time and solo outings to the movies, dinner, or even a cooking class can be empowering, and, believe it or not, ridiculously fun!

💙 Journaling can be a great way to process feelings and encourage self-love. Check out our five Calm Journals plus our Feelings Wheel to get you started.

Caring for your body and mind plays a major role in cultivating self-love. Simple acts like mindful eating, exercise, and making time to relax can make a big difference in your overall well-being.

In a recent development, take breaks when you need them: Remember to rest — even a micro-break can refresh and rejuvenate you. Want to amp up your rest break a notch? Take it outside. Being in nature can naturally calm and refresh your mind and body.

Practice relaxation: Use techniques like deep breathing or yoga to relax your body and focus on your breath.

Nourish your body: Fuel your body with nourishing food that makes you feel good.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Small acts of kindness and self-compassion can interrupt a cycle of self-criticism and release neurotransmitters that create a sense of wellbeing.

Some years ago, my daughter was beaten up at a kids’ gathering. I asked myself as a psychologist, “What happened to kindness? When did we lose it?”.

Industry observers note that I started to dig into the research. In the World Happiness Report, researchers looked at kindness as a factor contributing to happiness, and they developed a novel way to study the prevalence of kind acts. They tracked “lost” wallets to see if they were returned. They found that more people were helping strangers than was reported before the pandemic, which may be surprising.

It has been revealed that other social science studies found that measurably happier people live in areas where community members tend to donate more, volunteer their time, or help strangers. In other words, helping inspires more helping.

[Download: Get a Grip on Tough Emotions].

Recent findings suggest that what explains this kindness-happiness connection? In short, giving or receiving kindness kickstarts a “helper’s high” in our brains.

Research demonstrates that acts of kindness engage certain brain networks that release good chemicals like an internal pharmacy:.

Sources indicate that the dopamine from a helper’s high is different from the endorphin hit associated with running, gaming, or gambling, which keeps you wanting more. The dopamine generated in a helper’s high continues to produce positive feelings over time. The release of these neurotransmitters is especially helpful for people with ADHD who may struggle with emotional control, motivation, and stress.

Studies have shown that volunteering, even for one hour a week, can reduce inflammatory and stress cortisol responses, and even increase longevity. Volunteering is also considered a preventative action for loneliness and depression. Teens who volunteer outside their homes are more resilient and less likely to become depressed, according to research.

It has been revealed that helping people learn to be kind to themselves is my lifelong challenge as a clinical psychologist. We tend to prioritize other people’s needs over our own. But the research is clear on self-compassion: When you talk to yourself in a kinder way, or do kind things for yourself, you’re learning how to quiet that inner critic.

[Read: Self-Compassion: The Fresh ADHD Treatment].

Here are five practices to improve your self-compassion.

Tara Cousineau, Ph.D., is a clinical psychologist, meditation teacher, and self-described recovering perfectionist. She is the author of The Kindness Cure and The Perfectionist’s Dilemma.

You may fear that recharging will damage your relationships, but taking time to rest is the smart choice that allows you to show up as your best self in your relationships.

Sometimes the challenge isn’t making friends but discerning whether a particular person deserves space in your life.

#103855. How to lower your heart rate quickly (and keep it healthy)
